correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs correctly from the relative positive invertible operator. Rationalizing the triangular defect and applying Cauchy--Schwarz to \(A-mI\) and \(MI-A\) gives the global constants \(m/\sqrt M\) and \(M/\sqrt m\). Sharpness follows from orthogonal spectral vectors in arbitrarily small endpoint spectral windows: for \(p\)-orthonormal \(u,v\), \(\Delta_p(u,u+tv)=t^2/4+O(t^4)\), while for \(A\)-orthogonal endpoint vectors the \(q\)-defect coefficient is \(\beta/(4\sqrt\alpha)\), yielding the two endpoint ratios. Combining those exact defect constants with the pointwise norm ratios \(\sqrt m,\sqrt M\) in the published intrinsic-metric formula gives \(\log[(M/\sqrt m)/(m/\sqrt M)]=(3/2)\log(M/m)\). The continuous-spectrum case is handled by spectral subspaces, so no eigenvalue assumption is hidden.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies the complete intrinsic metric geometry of the natural Hilbertian subcone, with a dimension-free exact factor and sharp constants valid even for continuous spectrum. This is a structural result about the newly introduced metric, not a single numerical example.
residual_risks: Its significance is localized to the Hilbertian subcone of the full norm cone.

final_claim: For any two equivalent Hilbert norms \(p,q\) on a nonzero real Hilbert space, if \(q(x)^2=\langle Ax,x\rangle_p\) and \(m=\inf\sigma(A), M=\sup\sigma(A)\), then the sharp triangular-defect comparison is \[\frac{m}{\sqrt M}\Delta_p\le\Delta_q\le\frac{M}{\sqrt m}\Delta_p,\] and the intrinsic Hilbert distance in the cone of equivalent norms is exactly \(d_{\mathcal N}([p],[q])=\frac32\log(M/m)=3d_{\log}([p],[q])\).
limitations: The theorem concerns the Hilbertian subcone of equivalent norms, not arbitrary equivalent Banach norms.

The source preprint introducing the intrinsic norm-cone metric was too recent for a second independent full-text mirror to be recovered during this run; the accessible primary abstract and the audited package were therefore supplemented by explicit residual-risk notation.
